reference_fields: Fruit Notes Volume 11, January 31, 1946 archive article describing newer peach varieties and their possible value for Massachusetts growers

categories.name: Massachusetts peach variety notes from Fruit Notes 1946
categories.description: Fruit Notes summarizes newer peach varieties for Massachusetts growers, with comments on fruit quality, hardiness, season, and trial value

extractors.category: Massachusetts peach variety notes from Fruit Notes 1946

rows.name: Marigold
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Marigold as a yellow-fleshed, semi-cling to free peach with small to medium fruit, good quality, strong bud hardiness, and value as a very early peach for Massachusetts

rows.name: Fisher
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Fisher as a bud sport of Valiant with yellow semi-cling fruit, only fair quality, uneven ripening, very hardy wood, and reported bud hardiness

rows.name: Raritan Rose
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Raritan Rose, from Hale by Cumberland, as a newer New Jersey white-fleshed peach that is usually freestone, fair to good in quality, sometimes soft or stringy, fairly bud hardy, and worth trial

rows.name: Oriole
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Oriole as a yellow-fleshed freestone peach of good quality with small to medium fruit, a need for heavy thinning, and very hardy buds and wood, while noting that many growers object to its small size

rows.name: Redhaven
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Red Haven as a Michigan peach from Halehaven by Kalhaven, with yellow flesh, fruit that is free when fully ripe, a brilliant red blush, thick tough skin, very firm flesh, fair quality, heavy yield potential, and hardiness said to exceed Elberta but not South Haven or Rochester

rows.name: Golden Globe
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Golden Globe as a large, round, yellow-fleshed freestone peach of high quality, but notes that its buds are a bit tender for Massachusetts

rows.name: Triogem
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Triogem, from Hale by Marigold, as a newer New Jersey peach with yellow freestone fruit, very high quality, attractive appearance, a need for good soil, good culture, and heavy thinning, fair bud hardiness below Greensboro or Carman, good hanging ability, and susceptibility to brown rot

rows.name: Sunhigh
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Sunhigh, from Hale by 40 CS, as a newer New Jersey peach with yellow flesh, semi-cling to free flesh, very good quality, and bud hardiness probably a little better than Elberta, while warning that clinginess and its nearness to Halehaven season may limit its usefulness

rows.name: Goldeneast
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Goldeneast as a beautiful, extra large, fine flavored, yellow freestone peach that may fit a few unusually favorable Massachusetts sites, while generally being too tender in bud for the state

rows.name: Red Rose
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Red Rose, from Hale by Delicious, as a newer New Jersey white-fleshed freestone peach of good quality that is usually firm but sometimes soft and stringy, yields well, and is reported hardy in New Jersey

rows.name: Pacemaker
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Pacemaker, from Hale by Marigold, as a recent New Jersey introduction with very attractive yellow freestone fruit of very good quality, but probably too tender in bud for Massachusetts

rows.name: Summercrest
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Summercrest, from Hale by Cumberland, as a recent New Jersey peach with yellow freestone fruit of very good quality, fair attractiveness with occasional poor coloring, better performance on soils not too high in fertility, good yields, poor fruit hanging ability, and buds fairly hardy but below Greensboro or Carman

rows.name: Kalhaven
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Kalhaven, from Hale by Kalamazoo, as a recent Michigan introduction with yellow freestone fruit that tends to cling, fair flavor, good yields, and above-average hardiness in Michigan reports; Fruit Notes says Summercrest had the edge so far but Kalhaven seemed worth trial

rows.name: Sungold
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Sungold as an Iowa chance seedling reported to have carried a crop after -25 F, with yellow freestone fruit of very good quality, heavy cropping that needs considerable thinning, medium or slightly larger fruit, a semi-dwarf tree habit like J.H. Hale, and trial value

rows.name: White Hale
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes White Hale, a Hale open-pollinated seedling, as a large, round, attractive freestone Hale type with white flesh but not especially good quality; the article says its season is probably after Elberta rather than before, because the chart used only two crops and one ripened abnormally early
rows.harvest_time: probably after Elberta rather than before

rows.name: Fertile Hale
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Fertile Hale as a supposedly self-fertile sport of the self-sterile J.H. Hale, but cautions that fertile Hale sports reported from several states may not all be the same and that the variety in the College orchard had not been very impressive

rows.name: Afterglow
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Afterglow, from Hale by a New Jersey seedling, as a yellow-fleshed, fairly attractive freestone peach with better quality than Elberta, good yield, and hardiness above Elberta
rows.harvest_time: normal ripening season probably slightly later than shown in the chart
